rubric.novelty: Does the direction add a real architectural or evaluation contribution beyond existing agents?
rubric.testability: Can it be evaluated with available compute and logs?
rubric.paper_value: Would the results support a credible workshop or conference paper?
rubric.human_leverage: Does it test where human participation matters?
rubric.risk: Lower is better; high risk means weak evidence or excessive scope.

candidates.title: Human-Gated Agentic Tree Search for Automated Research
candidates.core_hypothesis: Adding structured human gates to AI Scientist-v2 tree search improves final paper quality by pruning weak branches and enriching promising ones.
candidates.related_work_gap: AI Scientist-v2 automates tree search but does not systematically evaluate human intervention placement.
candidates.minimal_experiment: Run matched research tasks with no human gates, idea-only gates, branch-selection gates, and claim-audit gates.
candidates.evaluation_target: Expert paper-quality score, unsupported-claim count, experiment budget wasted on discarded branches.
candidates.main_risk: Human feedback may be too subjective unless captured in a strict schema.

candidates.title: Co-Scientist Front-End for AI Scientist-v2
candidates.core_hypothesis: AI Co-Scientist-style debate before experiment generation yields stronger hypotheses than AI Scientist-v2 ideation alone.
candidates.related_work_gap: Existing systems separate hypothesis debate from full experiment/writeup loops.
candidates.minimal_experiment: Compare AI Scientist-v2 topic-file ideation against multi-agent hypothesis debate on the same benchmark tasks.
candidates.evaluation_target: Novelty, feasibility, evidence grounding, and downstream experiment success.
candidates.main_risk: The benefit may disappear once constrained by runnable benchmarks.

candidates.title: AlphaEvolve-Style Subproblem Optimization Inside Automated Research
candidates.core_hypothesis: Delegating machine-gradeable subproblems to evolutionary code search improves experiment results without requiring full-paper autonomy.
candidates.related_work_gap: AlphaEvolve shows strong code evolution, but integration into AI Scientist-v2-style paper loops is underexplored.
candidates.minimal_experiment: Use OpenEvolve on selected algorithmic or ML-pipeline components within a research task and compare against direct LLM edit search.
candidates.evaluation_target: Metric gain, number of valid candidate programs, wall-clock/API cost, paper-level usefulness.
candidates.main_risk: Local metric improvements may not change the final research conclusion.

candidates.title: Co-Pilot AI Scientist v3 End-to-End System
candidates.core_hypothesis: A unified co-pilot architecture with human creative nodes, automated experiments, and programmatic search can produce better papers than autonomous-only pipelines.
candidates.related_work_gap: Prior systems each cover one layer: hypothesis, experiment/paper automation, or program search.
candidates.minimal_experiment: Build an orchestration layer with logged human gates and run two small research tasks end to end.
candidates.evaluation_target: End-to-end reproducibility, expert review, benchmark results, and artifact completeness.
candidates.main_risk: Scope is large; requires careful staging to avoid a broad but weak paper.

reason: It is the narrowest experimentally defensible core contribution and can later absorb the Co-Scientist and AlphaEvolve components as modules.
